title: Digital Transformation Strengthens Livestock and Fisheries Sectors
subtitle: Bharat Pashudhan and NFDP Expand Digital Access, Services and Support for Farmers
body_text:
The Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh, stated that the Government is leveraging technology and digital platforms to strengthen the livestock and fisheries sectors and improve access to services for farmers, fishers and other stakeholders.
As on date number of livestock registered under the 12-digit unique identification system, ‘Pashu Aadhaar’, on the Bharat Pashudhan Portal is 39.23 crore.
As on date, 35.85 lakh fishers, fish farmers, fish vendors and other stakeholders have been registered on the National Fisheries Digital Platform (NFDP). The details of how the NFDP facilitates access to credit and insurance for registered stakeholders are provided.
There is no provision for processing of KCC application to be taken up under these digital ecosystems i.e. ‘Bharat Pashudhan’ for Animal Husbandry and NFDP for Fisheries. KCC application are processed and approved by banks through their core banking software systems.
The Government has launched Bharat Pashudhan, a technology-enabled, farmer-centric digital ecosystem that assigns every registered livestock animal a unique 12-digit barcoded ear tag for tracking breeding, health, ownership, and productivity-related information. Through mobile and web applications used across all States and UTs, field workers record activities such as animal registration, artificial insemination, vaccination, disease reporting, e-prescriptions, ration balancing, and milk recording. As on date, 17.27 crore artificial inseminations have been recorded under the Nationwide Artificial Insemination Programme (NAIP), covering 10.51 crore animals and benefiting 5.98 crore farmers. The platform also stores milk productivity data from genetic improvement programmes to support the selection of high genetic merit bovines. In addition, the 1962 Mobile App enables farmers to access authenticated livestock information and services using the same unique animal ID.
The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying is implementing a new Central Sector Sub-scheme namely the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY) under the ongoing Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) for a period of four years from FY 2023-24 to FY 2026-27 at an estimated outlay of ₹6,000 crore.
The National Fisheries Digital Platform (NFDP) under PM-MKSSY was launched on 11.09.2024. The NFDP aims at formalization of the Indian fisheries and aquaculture sector through creation of work-based digital identity and the database for all stakeholders in fisheries sector. It also serves as 'one-stop' solution for access to institutional credit, strengthening of fisheries co-operatives, incentivizing aquiculture insurance, performance-based incentives, fisheries' traceability systems and training and capacity building. As on date, 35.85 lakh fishers, fish farmers, fish vendors and other stakeholders have been registered on NFDP.
For facilitating easy access to benefit available under PMMKSSY including financial and technical support, the entire process of application by the intended beneficiaries has been made available online.
The PM-MKSSY under its component 1-A provides for enhancing access institutional credit to the fishers, fish farmers, fish workers, fish vendors, micro & small enterprises etc. Under NFDP, 12 nationalised banks have been on boarded. The lead applications received under NFDP is forwarded to banks. The bank takes further necessary action as per the laid down procedure. The financial assistance upto ₹5,000 is provided to the eligible beneficiary for successful loans.
Besides, the PM-MKSSY under its component 1-B also provides for one time incentive for purchase of aquaculture insurance by farmers. The one time incentive for aquaculture insurance is provided at the rate of 40% of the premium paid with a ceiling up to ₹25,000 per hectare, or ₹1 lakh per farmer for 4 hectares Water Spread Area (WSA). For the aquaculture system including intensive systems like farms, cage culture, RAS, bio-floc, and raceways etc. aquaculture insurance is provided at the rate of 40% of the premium paid with a ceiling up to ₹1 lakh per farmer for 1800 m3 for intensive aquaculture systems. Further, the SC/ST and women beneficiaries get an additional 10% of incentive.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying highlighted digital initiatives strengthening these sectors: the Bharat Pashudhan Portal has registered 39.23 crore livestock under a 12-digit 'Pashu Aadhaar' unique ID system, while the National Fisheries Digital Platform (NFDP) has registered 35.85 lakh fishers and stakeholders. Under Bharat Pashudhan, 17.27 crore artificial inseminations have been recorded benefiting 5.98 crore farmers. The NFDP, launched under PM-MKSSY (a ₹6,000 crore Central Sector Sub-scheme under PMMSY, FY2023-24 to FY2026-27), facilitates credit access, aquaculture insurance incentives, and traceability, though Kisan Credit Card applications are still processed only through banks' own systems.
enrichment.context:
Digital identity systems for agriculture and allied sectors have become a major governance tool in India, mirroring efforts like Aadhaar and the Agristack for crop farmers. Bharat Pashudhan, by tagging every registered animal with a unique ID, aims to formalize livestock management, enable traceability for disease control and breeding programmes, and support data-driven schemes like the Nationwide Artificial Insemination Programme, which is central to improving bovine genetics and milk productivity under the Rashtriya Gokul Mission ecosystem. This addresses long-standing challenges of unorganized record-keeping in India's vast unorganized livestock sector, which is significant given India is the world's largest milk producer.

Similarly, the fisheries sector has historically suffered from informality, with many fishers and fish farmers lacking documented identity, making it difficult for them to access institutional credit, insurance, or government subsidies. The NFDP, launched under PM-MKSSY (a sub-scheme of the flagship Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana), seeks to formalize this workforce by creating verifiable digital identities linked to credit facilitation, cooperative strengthening, and insurance incentives—particularly for aquaculture, a rapidly growing sub-sector. The scheme's insurance incentive structure, including higher incentives for SC/ST and women beneficiaries, reflects a broader push toward financial inclusion and social equity in blue economy initiatives, aligning with India's goals of doubling fisheries exports and incomes under PMMSY.

prelims_questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Bharat Pashudhan Portal:
1. It assigns a unique 12-digit ear tag ID to registered livestock.
2. It processes Kisan Credit Card (KCC) applications directly through the portal.
3. It records data related to artificial insemination, vaccination, and milk productivity.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: Bharat Pashudhan assigns unique 12-digit IDs and records AI, vaccination, and milk productivity data, but KCC applications are processed only by banks through their own core banking systems, not through the portal.

prelims_questions.question: The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY) is implemented as a sub-scheme under which of the following?
prelims_questions.explanation: PM-MKSSY is a Central Sector Sub-scheme implemented under the ongoing Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) for the period FY 2023-24 to FY 2026-27.

mains_questions.question: Discuss how digital identity systems like Bharat Pashudhan and the National Fisheries Digital Platform (NFDP) can help formalize India's livestock and fisheries sectors. What challenges remain in ensuring equitable access to institutional credit and insurance for small and marginal stakeholders?

mains_questions.question: Examine the role of digital governance platforms in strengthening last-mile delivery of welfare schemes in the primary sector, with reference to livestock and fisheries in India.
